record.field: In Odoo 17+, the field 'product_uom' was renamed to 'product_uom_id' on sale.order.line, purchase.order.line, and similar models.
Replace 'product_uom' with 'product_uom_id' in all code that creates or updates order lines.
In Odoo 17+, the field 'product_uom' was renamed to 'product_uom_id' on purchase.order.line.
Replace 'product_uom' with 'product_uom_id' when creating purchase order lines.

This error occurs when passing a wrong type to a field. Common causes: - Passing a string where an integer is expected (Many2one fields) - Passing an integer where a list is expected (One2many fields) - Wrong tuple format for One2many commands
Ensure correct types: - Many2one: Pass integer ID directly, not string - One2many: Use list of tuples [(0, 0, {...})] - Selection: Pass string value - Boolean: Use ${True} or ${False}
# WRONG - string instead of integer ${order_vals}= Create Dictionary ... partner_id="5" ... order_line=1
The 'bypass_access' parameter is not supported in this Odoo version or in JSON-RPC calls. This happens when using internal Odoo methods that expect different parameters.

Remove the bypass_access parameter. Use simpler search queries without access control parameters. If you need to bypass access rights, ensure the user has proper permissions or use sudo() in Python code.
# WRONG - bypass_access not supported in RPC ${ids}= Search Records product.product domain=[] bypass_access=True
# CORRECT - simple search without bypass_access ${ids}= Search Records product.product domain=[] limit=10
The test is trying to find an existing product with sale_ok=True, but the database has no such products. This commonly happens on empty or minimal test databases.
Create the required test data at the start of the test instead of searching for existing data. Always create test data - never assume data exists.
# WRONG - assumes data exists ${product_ids}= Search Records product.product domain=[('sale_ok','=',True)] Should Be True len(${product_ids}) > 0 msg=No saleable product found

# CORRECT - create test data ${product_id}= Create Record product.product ... name=QA Test Product ... type=consu ... sale_ok=${True} ... list_price=100.0
# Use the created product Should Be True ${product_id} > 0
The test is searching for existing partners/customers but the database has none or none matching the criteria.
Create test partner at the start of the test.
# WRONG - assumes partners exist ${partner_ids}= Search Records res.partner domain=[('is_company','=',True)] Should Be True len(${partner_ids}) > 0

# CORRECT - create test partner ${partner_id}= Create Record res.partner ... name=QA Test Company ... is_company=${True} ... email=test@example.com
# Use the created partner Should Be True ${partner_id} > 0
The test uses a custom keyword defined in *** Keywords *** section, but when the robot file is combined for Jenkins execution, the Keywords section may be stripped or not properly included.
Avoid using custom keywords. Put all logic directly inline in the test case. This makes tests self-contained and avoids keyword scope issues.

# WRONG - uses custom keyword that may not be found *** Keywords *** Create Test Data ${id}= Create Record res.partner name=Test Set Test Variable ${partner_id} ${id}
*** Test Cases *** My Test Create Test Data # May fail with "No keyword found"
# CORRECT - inline everything *** Test Cases *** My Test # Create data inline - no custom keyword needed ${partner_id}= Create Record res.partner name=QA Test Partner Should Be True ${partner_id} > 0
Trying to set a value on a readonly or computed field. Computed fields are automatically calculated by Odoo and cannot be set directly.
Remove the readonly field from the create/write values. Set the source fields that are used to compute the value instead.
# WRONG - trying to set computed field ${vals}= Create Dictionary ... name=Test Order ... amount_total=1500.00 # amount_total is computed! ${id}= Create Record sale.order &{vals}
A variable is used before being defined, or is used in teardown but may not have been created if the test failed early.
Initialize all variables at the start of the test with default values (like ${EMPTY}). This ensures teardown can safely reference them even if the test fails before they're set.
